Hi Karthik,

We're preparing Aurora's technical review packet for private deployments and need a concise 'risk heatmap' that maps likely operational scenarios to severity and mitigations (network egress, operator access, supply-chain/patching, telemetry retention, emergency rollback).

Also indicate if there are any on-call or SLA expectations for patch windows, emergency hotfixes, and key-rotation cadence. If you have a single doc or a couple of artifacts we can attach to the RFP, that would be helpful.

Subject: RE: Request: risk heatmap + operator handoff for private runtime evaluation

David — attaching the two artifacts you requested and summarizing key points inline.

Attachments (stubs):
- aurora-risk-heatmap-v2.xlsx (Excel spreadsheet)
- operator_handoff_checklist_v1.pdf (PDF checklist)

Executive summary (quick):
- Scope: private runtime deployed in Aurora VPC with optional airgap mode for selected sites. Heatmap maps five risk categories: Network Egress, Operator Access, Patch & Supply Chain, Telemetry & Data Retention, Emergency Rollback.
- Severity buckets: Critical / High / Medium / Low. We mark plausible event vectors and mitigations for each.

Heatmap highlights (abridged):
- Network egress (High): Risk = unauthorized outbound connections during model downloads or telemetry leaks. Mitigation = default-deny egress rules, allowlist endpoints for model pulls, explicit operator approval for any outbound tunnels.
- Operator access (High): Risk = privileged console access misuse. Mitigation = RBAC segregation, MFA for operator console, short-lived operator tokens, mandatory operator activity auditing.
- Patch & supply-chain (Medium): Risk = compromised package or kernel update in offline environments. Mitigation = signed artifacts, reproducible build checks, allowlist of update sources, offline validation workflow with checksum verification and operator acceptance tickets.
- Telemetry & retention (Medium): Risk = sensitive logs retained beyond policy. Mitigation = configurable telemetry filters, customer-controlled retention policy, ability to disable PII collection prior to export.
- Emergency rollback (Critical): Risk = failed model or runtime update causing degraded output. Mitigation = canary rollouts on dedicated pools, snapshot-backed KV cache restore, documented rollback command sequence, automatic fallback to smaller compatible model variant.

Operator handoff checklist (key items from attached PDF):
1) Identity & Access
  - Confirm RBAC groups and add initial on-call roster (names + emails)
  - Configure MFA policies for operator accounts
2) Network & Egress
  - Apply recommended egress allowlist and verify via staging tests
  - Validate no data-plane outbound flows to non-approved buckets
3) Patching & Supply Chain
  - Establish update cadence (recommended: quarterly for non-critical, emergency as-needed)
  - Install artifact-signing keys and test offline signature verification
  - Document rollback ticket and SRE escalation path
4) Telemetry & Logs
  - Set retention windows and sampling thresholds (example values in attachment)
  - Confirm local storage quotas and archival/ingest policies
5) Runbook & On-call
  - Import the runbook to your internal pagerduty/Jira (link in attachment)
  - Define SLOs and runbook trigger thresholds (latency per route, error-rate)

Notes on key rotation and SLA:
- We support BYOK (customer-managed KMS) for private installs; key-rotation cadence is at customer discretion. We recommend rotating data encryption keys every 90 days and signing keys every 180 days for offline environments; Redwood can support automation hooks if Aurora wants us to operate rotations under an agreed process.
- Patch windows: standard non-emergency patches are scheduled with 48–72 hour notice; emergency hotfixes follow a documented emergency-change process and are available 24/7 under a dedicated escalation path when you subscribe to enterprise support.

Operational artifacts: the attachments have the full heatmap matrix (aurora-risk-heatmap-v2.xlsx) and a one-page checklist with acceptance gates and dry-run steps (operator_handoff_checklist_v1.pdf). We uploaded a readable copy here: https://redwood-drive.example.com/shared/aurora-sandboxed-runtime-heatmap

If you want, we can run a 60-minute walkthrough next week and walk Aurora operators through the handoff checklist. Proposed slots: Tue 27 Jul 09:00-10:00 PT or Wed 28 Jul 13:00-14:00 PT.

—Marissa
